<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par118 />be regarded as originally a substantive<ref>Schwabe ({{GHGcite|title={{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} nach seinem Wesen und Gebrauch im alttestam. Kanon gewürdigt}}, Halle, 1883) contests this explanation (which is defended especially by Fleischer and is certainly indisputable). He, with Gesenius and Ewald, places {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a preposition on the same footing as {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, and believes it to be probably connected with the stem {{GHGheb|text=כּוּן}} as well as with {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=כֵּן}}. The above view of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a substantive of course does not imply that the language as we have it is still in every case conscious of the substantival meaning.—On {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} in numerical statements, in the sense of ''about, nearly'', see the Lexicon.</ref> in the sense of ''amount, kind'' (''instar''), standing in the accusative (so that {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is equivalent to ''as a kind of, after the manner of, according to''), while the following noun represents a genitive governed by the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}. From this, which is the proper meaning of the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, may be explained its power of representing a great many pregnant relations, which in English can only be rendered by the help of prepositions.<ref>It would be altogether unsuitable here also (see above, note 2 on r) to assume a loss of the preposition. Such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=26}} ({{GHGheb|text=כְּבָרִֽאשֹׁנָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=כְּבַתְּחִלָּה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=26|verse=37}} ({{GHGheb|text=כְּמִפְּנֵי}}) are to be explained from the fact that here the preposition and substantive had already become simply ''one'' word before the {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} was prefixed. We find also {{GHGheb|text=כְּעַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=14}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=32|verse=19}}; cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=כְּבַֽחֲצִי}}), where the text is wholly corrupt.</ref> Thus the comparison may refer to—

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|t}}
(''a'') The ''place'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is.|chapter=5|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּדָבְרָם|translate=after the manner of}}, i.e. ''as in their pasture''; 23:15 as (it is said) ''in the song of the harlot''; 28:21, 29:7 {{GHGheb|text=כּֽחֲלוֹם|translate=as in a dream}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|u}}
(''b'') The ''time'', especially in the combination {{GHGheb|text=כְּיוֹם|translate=after the manner of the day}}, equivalent to ''as in the day'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּימֵי|translate=as in the days of}} ..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=9|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=11}}; cf. moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, and the expressions {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם בְּיוֹם}} ''as day by day=as in the former days'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=כְּפַ֫עַם בְּפַ֫עַם|translate=as at other times}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=10}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=כְּשָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה|translate=as in former years}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=4}}; cf. {{GHGpar|123|c}}. Of a different character is the use of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} as a simple particle of time, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּעֵת חַיָּה|translate=at this time}} (not ''about the time''), when it lives again, i.e. at the end of a year; {{GHGheb|text=כָּעֵת מָחָר|translate=to-morrow at this time}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=5}}, and the frequent connexion of {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} with the infinitive construct to express a definite time (in the sense of a pluperfect), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=29}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|v}}
(''c'') The ''person'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=31}} ''should he deal with our sister as'' with ''a harlot?''

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|w}}
(''d'') The ''thing'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=28|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ|translate=as a fire}}, i.e. ''as it were by fire'' (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּבֹּר|translate=as}} with ''lye''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּטָר|translate=as}} for ''the rain'' (they waited for me); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=14}} (''as'' in ''a garment''); 38:30 {{GHGheb|text=כְּאֶבֶן|translate=as}} to ''stone'' (the waters are solidified in freezing).

{{GHGmargin-letter|118|x}}
Rem. According to the earlier grammarians, {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} is sometimes used pleonastically, i.e. not to indicate a similarity (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=35}} ''as it were'', i.e. ''something like''), but simply to introduce the predicate (''Kaph veritatis''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2}} ''for he was'' {{GHGheb|text=כְּאִישׁ אֱמֶת|translate=a faithful man}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּפֶשַׂע}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּ֫וֶת}}. Such a pleonasm is of course out of the question. At the most a ''Kaph veritatis'' can only be admitted in the sense that the comparison is sometimes introduced by {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}} with a certain emphasis (equivalent to ''in every respect like''); thus {{GHGheb|text=כְּאִישׁ אֱמֶת}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=2}} means simply ''of the nature of a faithful man'', i.e. as only a faithful man can be; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ob|chapter=1|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=2|verse=4|hidebook=1}}; also {{GHGheb|text=כִּמְעַט}} in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=105|verse=12}} ''yea, very few''; but e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=9}} ''only just, a very small''...<section end=par118 /><noinclude>
